purpose: dense, bright morning birdsong in a forest
author: bratendu
notes: 'Birds of Bengal' (Indian species). Spectrogram: many distinct overlapping calls 1-6 kHz throughout (trills, whistles, repeated notes), steady density across 25-89 s; start avoids the first 12 s (tonal hash lines 6-11 kHz) and the dip at 20 s. Source had broadband rumble below 150 Hz (not birds), removed with a 150 Hz 24 dB/oct high-pass before looping. Peak-limited to RMS -26 (birdsong is peaky). Chosen over 518671 (Essex woodland: good but European and less bright), 429048 (Himalayan dawn chorus: dominated by a steady 5-8 kHz insect band plus low rumble) and 787307 (Goa dawn: too sparse and quiet). 2026-10-01: constant hum lines at 98.7, 285.1 and 312.6 Hz notched (Q 20/30/30, zero-phase, filtered circularly over the loop body so the seam holds); lines now below the local noise floor, bird bands 1-12 kHz within 0.1 dB.

purpose: lighter garden birds with a soft leaf breeze
author: Sagnik_Basu
notes: Indian rural terrace, afternoon: light wind and leaf rustle with scattered varied bird calls 0.5-3 kHz. Per-second low-band scan used to place the window between a small bump at 126 s and a +7 dB low thump at 187-188 s (the loop tail ends at 185 s). Avoids the bang at ~55 s and the vehicle-like rumble in the first 50 s. RMS -26 (lighter bed). Chosen over 163997 (weak birds over low rumble) and 235782 (dominated by <150 Hz rumble). 2026-10-01: a harsh broadband knock at 38.80-39.02 s of the loop (+11 dB over the median, energy to 16 kHz) turned down 10 dB with 20 ms raised-cosine ramps; the 0.5 s tail (0-0.5 s) does not contain it.

purpose: gentle waves breaking on a sandy beach, close, clear wash-in/out rhythm
author: felix.blume
notes: Recorded close to the water on a beach near Lisbon. Spectrogram shows a regular break every 5-10 s (broadband swell to 6 kHz) with foamy wash between; no gulls, voices or wind rumble. Checked for clipping (max 0.94, no flat tops). Chosen over 629943 (lovely frothy rhythm but only 58.8 s, too short for a 60 s loop plus 4 s crossfade), 848039 (gentle but low wind rumble on the mic) and 711024 (small waves, thin and noisy).

purpose: open coastal distant surf rumble, a low bed under shore
author: TRP
notes: Medium rolling ocean surf heard from a distance: slow 4-6 s swells below 1.4 kHz with airy spray above, level even (5 s RMS within about 4 dB over the window). Sits lower, at RMS -28. Chosen over 870558 (a constant surf rumble with no life or air), 426074 (edit splice at 29 s) and 659004 and 640562 (energy mostly below 100 Hz, which suggests wind on the mic). No clean 'wind' recording without buffeting turned up, so this is surf-led. 2026-10-01: mixed to mono (64 kbps) to halve decoded memory; the mono sum is EQ'd back to the stereo pair's tonal balance and levelled to the same output power through its StereoPanner in nature.js.

purpose: waves lapping and splashing against rocks
author: TRP
notes: Waves on rocks, light crashing (Goderich). Spectrogram: a clear crash every 5-8 s whose spray reaches 11 kHz, with sloshing between; the whole file (4-68 s) is used. Chosen over 838667 (close sloshing, but a 32 dB crest factor means it can't reach -24 RMS), 451535 (Indian marina: light laps, low boat-like bump at 72 s), 841163 (thumpy, little spray) and 784465 (very quiet and muddy).

purpose: wind through trees on a hillside, distant birds
author: Garuda1982
notes: Windy pine forest with birds: a steady wind roar in the trees (200 Hz-2 kHz) with small distant birds at 3-8 kHz. Level is very even: 1 s low-band scan shows no step bigger than 1 dB, and the loop peak is -9 dBFS, so there are no gust buffets. Sub-100 Hz mic rumble was removed with a 100 Hz 24 dB/oct high-pass. Chosen over 751473 (nicer leaf rustle, but gust bursts at 45, 83 and 104 s carry 20-500 Hz buffet energy) and 384550 (palm wind with low buffets and a constant cricket tone). 2026-10-01: mixed to mono (64 kbps) to halve decoded memory; the mono sum is EQ'd back to the stereo pair's tonal balance and levelled to the same output power through its StereoPanner in nature.js.

purpose: steady rushing water from a dam spillway
author: leo153
notes: Water over a dam spillway: a dense full-band roar from 20 Hz to 10 kHz, dead steady (every 5 s window at -15 dB), no clipping (max 0.87). Chosen over 415997 (weir, similar but duller), 413737 (mono, a bird at 21 s and a change at 88 s) and 443870 (45 s, too short). 2026-10-01: mixed to mono (64 kbps) to halve decoded memory; the mono sum is EQ'd back to the stereo pair's tonal balance and levelled to the same output power through its StereoPanner in nature.js.

author: Funky_Audio
notes: Close-up of a small babbling stream: dense gurgles and bubbles at 200-1500 Hz, a sparkle to 6 kHz, almost nothing below 150 Hz, and level steady within 2 dB. Start 30 avoids a small peak at 25 s. Chosen over 715694 (brook with birds and peaks) and 559955 / 757969 (thinner, with more low rumble).

author: felix.blume
notes: Tropical night chorus (French Guiana rainforest): two dense insect bands at ~2.5 kHz and ~5 kHz, a soft frog and forest bed below, level steady within 3 dB. The window 5-69 s stays before the click-like broadband calls from 75 s and the low thump at 135 s. Sits lower, at RMS -27. Chosen over 571078 (a clean layered cricket chorus, but temperate, with bands that switch off at 57 and 93 s) and 751472 (one very loud close cricket, monotonous). 2026-10-01: mixed to mono (64 kbps) to halve decoded memory; the mono sum is EQ'd back to the stereo pair's tonal balance and levelled to the same output power through its StereoPanner in nature.js.
